stances.claim: Belgica v Ochoa (Nov 19, 2013) struck down PDAF as unconstitutional -- empowering legislators to specify projects from lump sums AFTER the GAA becomes law violates separation of powers; legislators cannot determine projects, authorize fund releases, or identify implementing agencies/NGOs post-enactment, except through congressional oversight.

The 'specific appropriation, stated purpose' rule bans lump-sum appropriations except for calamity, contingency, and intelligence funds -- meaning neither the president nor legislators have post-enactment power to determine how such lump sums shall be spent, with the rule designed to prevent graft.

Araullo v Aquino (July 1, 2014) declared four DAP acts unconstitutional (NOT the DAP itself): (1) transferring funds prior to fiscal year end without meeting any savings criteria; (2) cross-border transfers from executive to Congress/Comelec/COA; (3) funding PAPs not covered by any GAA appropriation; (4) using unprogrammed funds absent national-treasurer revenue certification -- all four violate the appropriation-by-law and no-transfer rules of the Constitution.

The power of augmentation is a limited constitutional exception -- only specified officials (President, Senate President, House Speaker, CJ, heads of Constitutional Commissions) can augment items in their respective offices from 'actual savings' (defined three ways), and crucially only within the same branch -- making cross-branch transfers categorically unconstitutional.
stances.rhetorical_move: exception-narrowness framing (limited officials + actual savings + same-branch only)

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban analyzes the Duterte administration's proposed P3.35 trillion 'budget for real change' for 2017 (11.6% larger than the P3.002 trillion 2016 outlay), with bulk going to infrastructures (airports, seaports, railways, roads) and human capital (education, health, social welfare). DepEd gets the biggest share at P570.4 billion (+31%); the judiciary's share rises from P26.79 billion to P32.54 billion, with CJ Sereno requesting 50 more family courts (added to 48 funded in 2016 -- the courts were created by law in 1997 but funded only starting 2016) and child-friendly equipment. Some lawmakers allege the budget is peppered with the graft-prone Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) and discredited Disbursement Acceleration Program (DAP) -- vehemently denied by Diokno and Alvarez -- stemming from each lawmaker being asked to submit a DBM list of P80M projects. To test the allegation, CJ revisits two SC decisions: Belgica v Ochoa (Nov 19, 2013, J Perlas-Bernabe ponente) struck down PDAF because empowering legislators to specify projects from lump sums AFTER the GAA becomes law violates separation of powers (legislators cannot determine projects, authorize releases, or identify implementing agencies/NGOs post-enactment, except via congressional oversight); the Court enunciated the 'specific appropriation, stated purpose' rule banning lump sums except calamity, contingency, and intelligence funds -- designed to prevent graft. Pre-enactment proposals during DBM drafting and pending congressional consideration remain proper. Araullo v Aquino (July 1, 2014, J Bersamin ponente) declared four DAP acts unconstitutional (not the DAP itself): (1) transferring funds prior to fiscal year end without meeting savings criteria; (2) cross-border transfers from executive to Congress/Comelec/COA; (3) funding PAPs not covered by any GAA appropriation; and (4) using unprogrammed funds absent the national treasurer's revenue-collection certification. The constitutional baseline is strict: 'No public money shall be paid out of the Treasury except in pursuance of an appropriation made by law' and 'No law shall be passed authorizing the transfer of appropriations.' The limited exception is the power of augmentation, allowing only the President, Senate President, House Speaker, Chief Justice, and heads of Constitutional Commissions to augment items in their respective offices from 'actual savings' (defined three ways: PAP completed/discontinued/abandoned; vacant positions or unpaid leaves; targets realized at lesser cost via improved systems and efficiencies) and only within the same branch.
